dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: We're not in any hurry to get going, are we? Let's chill here for a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: "When the cat's away, the mice will play." And so they should — 'cause it's only a matter of time before the cat gets back and gobbles all the mice up.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: So like I said — no need to hurry. The mice will be there for us when we're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: The look on your face tells me you're ready to head deeper into the domain. Next stop, the belly of the beast, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Never fear, for Director Hu Tao is here, ready to face whatever comes at us, from the ordinary, to the abnormal, to the paranormal!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: So, without further ado — shall we? Let's not keep the monsters waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Once I was old enough, I started reading popular novels. Some of them would end by having the dead come back to life and living happily ever after.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Tut-tut-tut... I know it's only make-believe, but still, it always ruined the story for me. If death isn't final, there are no stakes, so it kinda makes everything that happened up to that point meaningless.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: "To everything there is a season: Live in life, and die in death." That is the truth. You can't have a satisfactory ending if death isn't final.
